chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any dhimmi who buys land from a Muslim, then khums is upon him.'

key_terms.ذِمِّيٍّ: Dhimmi, a non-Muslim citizen living under Islamic rule

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on khums for a non-Muslim buying land from a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the khums obligation on land acquisition applies specifically to the non-Muslim buyer (dhimmi) when purchasing from a Muslim, a ruling often discussed in the context of the five categories of wealth subject to khums. It highlights the distinct fiscal responsibilities of dhimmis within the Islamic economic framework, distinguishing their transactional liabilities from those of Muslims. This specific narration underscores the practical application of khums in real estate, a key component of the 'zayadat' (increases) chapter.
